## Natural history notes

A large wolf spider characterized by its brown to grayish-brown body, long legs, and darker markings that help it blend into leaf litter, soil, and low vegetation. In Florida, it is found in pine flatwoods, scrub, hammocks, forest edges, fields, and other ground-level habitats with vegetation or debris for cover. Unlike many wolf spiders, it builds a funnel-like sheet web close to the ground and waits near the retreat entrance to ambush small insects and other arthropods that move across the web.
